skill.name: just-scrape
skill.description: Search, scrape, crawl, extract structured data, and monitor web pages with the ScrapeGraph AI just-scrape CLI.
skill.summary: Use the ScrapeGraph AI CLI for web search, scraping, crawling, structured extraction, and page monitoring.
skill.author: scrapegraphai

security_audit.summary: The static findings are mostly false positives caused by Markdown backticks, documented CLI commands, expected API key names, and example URLs. No prompt injection or covert credential exfiltration was found in SKILL.md. The remaining concern is an unpinned global npm install path for a community CLI package.

remediation.suggestion: Pin just-scrape to a reviewed version and avoid automatic global installs. Ask users to confirm package installation before running it.

remediation.issue: Sensitive headers and cookies can be passed to scraping commands
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before sending tokens, cookies, or private URLs to ScrapeGraph AI. Mask these values in logs and saved summaries.

remediation.issue: API key troubleshooting can expose secret values
remediation.suggestion: Use validation commands and masked diagnostics instead of printing SGAI_API_KEY, .env contents, or ScrapeGraph config files.

remediation.issue: Broad crawl and monitor operations can consume credits quickly
remediation.suggestion: Set page, depth, include-pattern, and monitor limits before running broad operations. Confirm expected cost with the user first.

semantic_findings.description: The skill advises installing the moving npm package just-scrape@latest globally or through npx. A changing community package can run new install-time code and alter behavior without review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The install commands are explicit and cite @latest, including a global npm install. This is likely intended setup behavior, but it creates supply-chain and reproducibility risk.

content.user_title: Extract Web Data with Just Scrape
content.value_statement: Manual web research and scraping can be slow and inconsistent. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through ScrapeGraph CLI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Search the web with result limits, country filters, time ranges, and optional structured extraction.
Scrape known URLs into markdown, HTML, screenshots, links, images, summaries, branding, or JSON.
Extract structured fields from pages using prompts and optional schemas.
Crawl bounded site sections with page limits, depth limits, and include or exclude patterns.
Create, inspect, update, pause, resume, and delete page monitors.
Check request history, credit balance, and API setup with CLI commands.
limitations: Requires the just-scrape CLI and a valid ScrapeGraph AI API key.
Consumes ScrapeGraph credits for searches, scrapes, crawls, and monitors.
Results depend on website access, robots policies, JavaScript rendering, and page stability.
Sensitive headers, cookies, and scraped content need careful handling outside the skill.

use_cases.title: Research Competitor Pages
use_cases.description: Find public pages, scrape visible content, and summarize pricing, positioning, or feature changes.

use_cases.title: Collect Documentation Content
use_cases.description: Crawl a bounded documentation section and save markdown or links for review, migration, or support answers.

use_cases.title: Monitor Page Changes
use_cases.description: Create recurring checks for public pages and inspect monitor activity when content changes.

prompt_templates.title: Scrape One Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use just-scrape to scrape this URL as markdown and summarize the main points. Save the raw output under .just-scrape.

prompt_templates.title: Search Before Scraping
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the web for recent sources about this topic. Return the best sources with titles, URLs, and a short reason for each.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Structured Fields
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract product names, prices, availability, and source URLs from this page. Use a strict schema and note missing fields.

prompt_templates.title: Crawl and Monitor Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Crawl this documentation section with clear page and depth limits. Then suggest a monitor plan for the pages most likely to change.

output_examples.input: Scrape a pricing page and summarize the plans.
output: Saved the raw scrape result under .just-scrape for later review.
Returned plan names, visible prices, limits, and the source URL.
Flagged missing details that need manual confirmation.

output_examples.input: Find sources about a market topic before analysis.
output: Returned a ranked source list with titles and URLs.
Explained why each source looked relevant.
Suggested which pages should be scraped next.
Created a bounded monitor plan with interval and page format.
Explained expected credit usage and review steps.
Listed commands for checking activity and pausing the monitor.

best_practices: Confirm the target URL and data fields before running high-credit operations.
Set crawl limits and include patterns before scraping site sections.
Store outputs in .just-scrape and review large files incrementally.
anti_patterns: Do not scrape protected pages with session cookies unless the user owns the access.
Do not run broad crawls or many monitors without explicit limits.
Do not paste API keys, bearer tokens, or cookies into prompts or logs.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires SGAI_API_KEY or a ScrapeGraph AI configuration before real requests can run.

faq.question: Can it scrape JavaScript-heavy pages?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill can guide JavaScript rendering, stealth mode, and scrolling options when simple scraping is incomplete.

faq.question: Can it return structured data?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports prompt-based extraction and optional schemas for stricter field output.

faq.question: Where should output files go?
faq.answer: The skill recommends saving raw outputs under .just-scrape and reading large files incrementally.

faq.question: Can it manage monitors?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers monitor creation, listing, updates, activity checks, pause, resume, and deletion.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Keep keys, bearer tokens, and cookies in environment variables or secure config. Do not print them in logs or summaries.
